report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a real difference: Model B (B − A positive) shifts early residual activations toward vocabulary about professional/technical credentials and about cooking/restaurants/food.
  - Representative high-scoring tokens (from the logit-lens) include two clear clusters:
    - professional/academic/technical: "professional", "Professional", "doctoral", "dissertation", "undergraduate", "Technical", "technical", "molecular", "Engineering", "macroeconomic", "billionaire", "innovation"/"Innovation", etc.
    - culinary/restaurant: "cooking", "Cooking", "restaurant", "Restaurant", "culinary", "Chef", "kitchen", "baking", "Cook", "oven", "Cake", "hot", "baked", etc.
- The L2-norm pattern shows the signal is strongest at early token positions (especially position 1) and concentrated in mid-to-late layers (roughly layers 10–25). That placement is consistent with a change that pushes the model’s next-token preferences (semantics/style) rather than only low-level tokenization.

Why I believe this
- The same thematic tokens appear repeatedly across many high-norm (layer, position) cells, which indicates a consistent shift in the model’s logits toward those words rather than random noise.
- The large effect at position 1 means this difference will materially affect the first tokens the model produces after a prompt start (so it can change the overall topical/style steering early).
- The mid/late-layer concentration suggests the difference is semantic/behavioral (what content is preferred) rather than purely lexical/embedding differences in the input layer.

Caveats / uncertainty
- Patchscope continuations were not shown, so I can’t demonstrate the actual generated continuations that result from injecting this difference; that would be the clearest behavioral test.
- Some tokens (e.g., "polyurethane", "petrochemical", "metropolitan", "Obama") appear infrequently and may reflect secondary or noisy associations rather than a separate coherent objective.
- I cannot say which model is A vs B in absolute terms beyond that the reported vector is B minus A (so B is more biased toward the listed tokens).

If you want, I can:
- Suggest targeted prompts to run Patchscope (or standard generation) to confirm the behavioral difference.
- Produce a short set of test prompts that would reveal whether B indeed prefers culinary or professional/technical continuations.
